latin.449: Quid enim? putasne ista verba, quia paruisti voci uxoris tuae, tibi, tuae, inquam, personae dicta esse, & ad te immediate spectare? Nonne vides quam personale fuit, & proprium Adamo, maritum fuisse Evae, tam ad eius personam accommodata esse haec verba? Potuitne Dei sententia verbis concipi magis, ut ita loquar, personalibus, magis propriis personae Adami, minus communibus generi humano?
latin.450: Id autem noli putare factum esse ab eo temere. Si Deus actuale illud peccatum Adami imputavisset hominibus nondum existentibus, eosque omnes immediate ob illud peccatum sua sententia poenis illis adjudicasset, qua est sapientia communem sententiam verbis communibus, & quae omnibus & singulis hominibus applicari possent, concepisset, aut posterorum Adami aliquam mentionem injecisset.
latin.451: Nunc autem Contrarium fecit, quorsum, nisi ut intelligamus decretas ea sententia poenas ad nos non pertinere, nisi quia Adamus nobiscum eas communicavit, communicata, quae illas meretur, per carnalem generationem peccati sui malitia? atque ita causam cur eas poenas luamus, non quaeramus in Deo nobis actionem, quam nullo modo commisimus, imputante, ut nos puniat, sed in Adamo solo, & natura peccati ipsius, quod, ut fermentum quoddam massae generis humani immissum, eam totam, non per Dei imputationem, sed per carnalem generationem corrupit, ac malitia infecit. Vides me Dei causam agere, noli quaeso ei adversari.
latin.452: Me enim vehementer offendit, quod tu, & alii quidam fratres nostri, dicitis, Deum omnes homines, etiam puerulos, punire morte corporis (& aeterna) immo morte animae, quae formaliter peccatum est, ob peccatum actuale quod eorum non est ullo modo, nisi imputatione, quia Deus illud ipsis imputat. Id vel cogitare horret conscientia, ac ut aliam tibi & illis mentem det, Dominum supplex ex animo precor.
latin.453: Quo enim jure, ut ait alicubi Bellarminus (cui tecum haec causa est communis) mihi imputatur, quod meum non est? quae haec justitia, peccatum quod alioqui omnium commune non est, imputando omnibus commune facere, ac propterea omnes homines tam severe punire? Non est, inquis, primum illud peccatum commune omnibus, nisi imputatione, quia scilicet omnibus imputatur. Ergo inquam, antequam imputetur omnibus, commune non est omnibus. Quod igitur commune est omnibus, id soli isti imputationi, quae scilicet actio Dei est judiciaria, imputandum est.
latin.454: Considera, quaeso, quae sit falsa & injusta imputatio, si haec non est; Et, an conveniat Deo actio, quae nos alioqui non peccatores, peccatores faciat, & quidem formaliter, & per se, & annon hoc sit causam omnium nostrorum peccatorum & malorum in Deum referre; & da gloriam creatori tuo & redemptori. Revoca in animum quae dixi Cap. 3. hujus examinis §. III. Neque puta tuam illam sententiam esse ex fontibus vel patrum antiquorum, vel eorum qui primi & praecipue manum admoverunt Ecclesiae Reformandae seculo superiore, haustam & deductam. Longe aliter illi senserunt, ut, Deo dante, faciam alio Capite manifestum. Nunc mihi satis est tuorum argumentorum nodos solvere.

pass_a.449: So what? Are 'because you obeyed your wife's voice' meant as addressed to you—to your person—and aimed at you right away? See how personal that was, how proper to Adam as Eve's husband, how those words fit his person. Could the divine sentence have been cast in speech more personal to Adam, more his own, less shared with humankind?
pass_a.450: Do not call that rash. Had God charged Adam's actual sin to humans not yet in being and by sentence at once sentenced them all to those pains for it, wisdom would have framed a shared sentence in shared words that fit every person, or named Adam's posterity.
pass_a.451: He did the opposite instead. Why, unless so we grasp that the pains fixed in that sentence touch us only because Adam shared them with us—his sin's desert-making malice passed along by fleshly generation? Seek the reason we suffer those pains not in God charging us with a deed we never did so he may punish us, but in Adam alone and in that sin's nature: like yeast worked into the dough of humankind it spoiled the whole loaf not by divine imputation but by fleshly generation, and tainted it with malice. Placeus is defending God's cause—please do not fight him.
pass_a.452: It deeply offends Placeus that you and certain other brothers say God punishes all humans, even little children, with bodily (and eternal) death—indeed with death of the soul, which formally is sin—for an actual sin that is theirs in no way except by imputation, because God imputes it to them. Conscience shudders even to think it, and Placeus earnestly begs the Lord to give you and them another mind.
pass_a.453: Bellarmine asks somewhere—and you share his cause here—by what right is what is not mine charged to me? What justice turns a sin not otherwise everyone's into everyone's by charging it to all, then punishes all so hard? You claim that first sin is common to all only by imputation, since it is charged to all. Then, says Placeus, before that charge it is not common to all. So whatever is common to all must be put down to that charge alone—God's act as judge.
pass_a.454: Consider, please, what false and unjust imputation would be, if this is not; and whether an action befits God that makes us sinners who otherwise were not—and formally and of itself—and whether that is not to refer the cause of all our sins and evils to God; give glory to your creator and redeemer. Recall what Placeus said in Cap. 3 of this examination § III. Do not think your view is drawn from the ancient fathers or from those who first chiefly set hand to reforming the Church in the last century. They thought far otherwise, as God willing he will make plain in another chapter. For now it is enough to untie your arguments' knots. Tip before the Gospel-promise / seed-of-the-woman argument.

449: What then? Do you think those words—because you obeyed your wife's voice—were spoken to you, to your person, I say, and look to you immediately? Do you not see how personal it was, and proper to Adam, that he was Eve's husband, how fitted to his person these words are? Could God's sentence have been conceived in words more, so to speak, personal, more proper to Adam's person, less common to the human race?
450: But do not think that was done by him rashly. If God had imputed that actual sin of Adam to humans not yet existing, and by his sentence had immediately adjudged them all to those penalties for that sin, with what wisdom would he have conceived a common sentence in common words, and such as could be applied to all and each human, or would he have injected some mention of Adam's posterity.
451: But now he did the Contrary—to what end, unless that we understand the penalties decreed by that sentence do not pertain to us, except because Adam communicated them with us, the malice of his sin which merits them having been communicated through carnal generation? and so that we should not seek the cause why we pay those penalties in God imputing to us an action which we in no way committed, that he may punish us, but in Adam alone, and in the nature of the sin itself, which, like some leaven put into the mass of the human race, corrupted that whole mass not through God's imputation but through carnal generation, and infected it with malice. You see that I am pleading God's cause; do not, I beg you, oppose him.
452: For it vehemently offends me that you, and certain other brothers of ours, say that God punishes all humans, even little children, with death of the body (and eternal), indeed with death of the soul, which formally is sin, for an actual sin which is theirs in no way, except by imputation, because God imputes it to them. Conscience shudders even to think it, and that he may give you and them another mind, I earnestly beg the Lord from the heart.
453: For by what right, as Bellarmine says somewhere (with whom this cause is common with you), is what is not mine imputed to me? What is this justice—by imputing to make common to all a sin which otherwise is not common to all, and therefore to punish all humans so severely? That first sin, you say, is not common to all except by imputation, because namely it is imputed to all. Therefore, I say, before it is imputed to all, it is not common to all. What therefore is common to all must be credited to that imputation alone, which namely is God's judicial act.
454: Consider, I beg you, what a false and unjust imputation would be, if this is not; And whether an action befits God which makes us sinners who otherwise were not sinners, and indeed formally, and of itself, and whether this is not to refer the cause of all our sins and evils to God; and give glory to your creator and redeemer. Call back to mind what I said in Cap. 3 of this examination § III. And do not think that opinion of yours was drawn and deduced from the fountains either of the ancient fathers, or of those who first and chiefly set hand to reforming the Church in the last century. Far otherwise did they think, as, God granting, I shall make plain in another Chapter. For now it is enough for me to untie the knots of your arguments.
